segments: Malik Mas'ud.
And as if by a satanic instigation,
this Mas'ud intensely hated the daughter of Badr al-Din.
And al-Mu'azzam, his father, admonished him greatly
not to reveal [his] hatred,
but he was unable [to hide it].
And when the daughter began to complain to Badr al-Din, her father,
he sent [and] took her [back].
And after a little while, al-Mu'azzam died,
and Malik Mas'ud, his son, arose in his place.
And Badr al-Din began to press him with claims,
to the point that he would send and say to him:
"I want such-and-such a signet-ring that is on the finger of such-and-such woman (a maidservant) by name,
and such-and-such and such-and-such of such-and-such woman."
And while he was giving everything,
finally he sent to him:
"You, for your part, sold {OCR?} Jazira when we were encamped against Nisibis."
And Mas'ud sent to him:
"Everything I have accepted from you,
yes; but to give you my kingdom, I cannot do that."
Therefore, Badr al-Din gathered armies
and went and encamped against Jazira on Tuesday the 24th {OCR?}
in the sixth month of the said year, in the days of Nisan,
and he pressed it hard in battle.
And Mas'ud sent and asked for a promise [of safety] for his life.
And Badr al-Din promised him that he would give him the fortress called Farrah,
so that he might take his household and his women and go away.
And Mas'ud agreed,
and made the guards and fighters withdraw {OCR?} from it.
And Badr al-Din sent one of his eunuchs, who cast irons upon him,
and took him out by night from Jazira and seated him in a boat,
as though he were sending him to Mosul.
And he commanded the sailors and the servants whom he placed with him to drown him in the Tigris,
and to abandon [everything] and flee to Syria,
and spread the report: "This Mas'ud threw himself into the river and was drowned,
and we feared our master Badr al-Din, lest he destroy us
because we were negligent regarding him when he did this to himself."
And when they took him and went down to sail on the Tigris, they did as they were commanded,
and fled to Syria,
and spread this rumor;
and after a year, they returned again to Mosul.
As for that Badr al-Din, he entered Jazira and took possession of it on Friday the eleventh in the seventh month of the said year.
This city was not of Greek construction,
but certain Ma'addite people who were called the Banu 'Umar built it.
